Q64818.label: 2011 Polish parliamentary election
Q64818.summary: Parliamentary elections were held in Poland on 9 October 2011. All 460 members of the Sejm and 100 senators of the Senate were elected. The ruling Civic Platform (PO) won a plurality of seats and Tusk became the first Polish prime minister to be appointed for a second consecutive term since the fall of communism.

Q460082.label: 1962 Austrian legislative election
Q460082.summary: Parliamentary elections were held in Austria on 18 November 1962. The result was a victory for the Austrian People's Party, which won 81 of the 165 seats. Voter turnout was 94%. Although the People's Party had come up only two seats short of an outright majority, Chancellor Alfons Gorbach retained the grand coalition with the Socialists under Vice-Chancellor Bruno Pittermann.

Q192818.label: Bettino Craxi
Q192818.summary: Benedetto "Bettino" Craxi was an Italian politician and statesman, leader of the Italian Socialist Party (PSI) from 1976 to 1993, and the 45th prime minister of Italy from 1983 to 1987. He was the first PSI member to become prime minister and the second from a socialist party to hold the office.

Q84027698.label: 2024 Croatian presidential election
Q84027698.summary: Presidential elections were held in Croatia on 29 December 2024, with a second round held on 12 January 2025 after no candidate received a majority of the vote in the first round. Incumbent president Zoran Milanović was eligible for a second term, and was re-elected with a record 75% of the vote.

Q117442866.label: 2027 Finnish parliamentary election
Q117442866.desc: Parliamentary elections will be held in Finland on 18 April 2027 to elect members of parliament for the 2027–2031 term
Q117442866.summary: Parliamentary elections will be held in Finland on 18 April 2027 to elect members of parliament for the 2027–2031 term. It will be the first parliamentary election in Finland since the country acceded to NATO on 4 April 2023, ending 75 years of military non-alignment for the country.

Q140735282.label: 2026 Kumamoto earthquake
Q140735282.img: 20260730 Track Damage of Kagoshima Line (Matsubase - Ogawa).jpg
Q140735282.summary: On 28 July 2026 at approximately 16:27:15 JST, an earthquake struck Kumamoto Prefecture in southern Japan with a magnitude of Mww 6.8 at a depth of 10 km (6.2 mi), later revised to 16 km (9.9 mi). At least 38 people were killed and more than 368 were injured.

Q441650.label: Popular Alliance
Q441650.summary: The Popular Alliance was a liberal-centrist political party in San Marino. The party formed a coalition with the Union for the Republic for the 2016 Sammarinese general election, and following their electoral success the two parties created a new party, Future Republic.

Q189746.label: Islamism
Q189746.desc: political ideology for applying Islamic doctrine to politics and society
Q189746.summary: Islamism is a range of religious and political ideological movements that believe that Islam should influence political systems. Its proponents believe Islam is innately political, and that Islam as a political system is superior to communism, liberal democracy, capitalism, and other alternatives in achieving a just, successful society. The advocates of Islamism are usually affiliated with Islamic institutions or social mobilization movements, emphasizing the implementation of sharia, pan-Islamic political unity, and the creation of Islamic states.
